question: Gastric irritation is least with following NSA1D: (PGI June 2008)
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Acetaminophen" -> "minimal COX inhibition in stomach" -> "least gastric irritation" -> 95%
analysis: The question asks which drug causes the least gastric irritation among the given options. Acetaminophen (opb) is not a traditional NSAID and primarily acts as an analgesic and antipyretic. It has minimal inhibition of cyclooxygenase (COX) enzymes in the stomach, which are responsible for the production of protective gastric prostaglandins. This results in minimal gastric irritation compared to traditional NSAIDs. Diclofenac (opa), Ibuprofen (opc), and Naproxen (opd) are all NSAIDs that inhibit COX enzymes, leading to varying degrees of gastric irritation. Among these, Naproxen is known to cause more gastric irritation due to stronger COX inhibition. Therefore, based on standard medical knowledge and consensus, Acetaminophen is the least likely to cause gastric irritation among the options.
